attempts.summary: Configured a DHCP relay chain so node3 (isolated on node1's eth2 segment) obtains its address from node2's DHCP service (isolated on node1's eth1 segment). Built out the missing segments (192.168.10.0/24 between node1↔node2, 192.168.20.0/24 between node1↔node2's DHCP-served node3 segment), installed and configured dnsmasq on node2 as the DHCP server for 192.168.20.0/24, installed and configured isc-dhcp-relay (dhcrelay) on node1 to relay broadcasts between eth1 and eth2, and added the return route on node2 (via node1) so DHCPOFFER/ACK unicast replies reach the relay's giaddr. All configuration was made persistent (static /etc/network/interfaces.d entries and sysctls on node1, static interface + boot route script on node2, dhcp-on-boot on node3), and verified across a full one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes with new boot IDs and automatic post-reboot recovery of the relay chain (node3 re-acquired lease 192.168.20.139 fully automatically after its own reboot).
